topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate Immune Recognition: PAMPs, DAMPs, and Pattern Recognition Receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms and receptor pathways used by the innate immune system to recognize pathogens and cellular damage.

topics.label: The Acute Inflammatory Cascade, Leukocyte Trafficking, and Systemic Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the cellular execution of acute inflammation, covering leukocyte recruitment and trafficking, adaptive priming via lymphatics, and the danger of septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammatory States
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the passive and active mechanisms that resolve inflammation, tissue repair processes, and the development and function of chronic inflammation and granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and announces the topic of the next lecture.
